scores.claim_text: iRobot has sold over 50 million consumer robots worldwide since the Roomba introduction in 2002.
scores.M_value: 538 granted patents, 945 total applications; top recent applications include 'MOBILE CLEANING ROBOT', 'CONTROL OF AUTONOMOUS MOBILE ROBOTS', 'ROBOT LOCALIZATION AND MAPPING', 'TWO IN ONE MOBILE CLEANING ROBOT', 'WASHABLE BIN FOR A ROBOT VACUUM CLEANER' — all consistent with consumer robotic vacuum business at scale
scores.interpretation: Cumulative-units claim is unverifiable directly from public M-sources, but 23-year operating history with 538 granted patents in the relevant product CPC classes (A47L vacuum cleaners, G05D robot motion control) plus disclosed $681.8M FY2024 revenue + $1.18B FY2022 revenue is consistent with very large historical unit shipments. No contradiction. PASS.

scores.claim_text: One customer accounted for 22.2% of total revenue in fiscal 2024 (24.0% in 2023, 22.6% in 2022).
scores.M_value: Amazon (AMZN, CIK 1018724): 7 hits — but all in 2022-2024 context of the now-terminated merger agreement (8-K, 10-Q, 10-K disclosures of the iRobot acquisition deal), NOT customer-relationship disclosure. Walmart (WMT): 0 hits. Target (TGT): 0 hits.
scores.interpretation: The 22.2% customer is unnamed in iRobot's 10-K (only required to disclose if a single customer >10%; name not required by GAAP). At ~$151M of annual revenue (22.2% of $681.8M), this is material to iRobot but immaterial to any megacap retailer (Amazon retail GMV >$500B, Walmart ~$650B revenue), so the customer would NOT have a counterparty-disclosure obligation under Layer 3 Rule 7. Heuristic 7 second branch applies: 'ABSENCE for a relationship where the customer has no recognition obligation' = no contradiction. However, the company is NOT naming the customer despite multi-year >20% concentration, which is a moderate-weight disclosure-completeness concern given the Amazon-merger backdrop (the 22% customer could plausibly be Amazon retail). Score MODERATE.

scores.claim_text: On January 28, 2024, iRobot and Amazon mutually terminated the merger agreement; Amazon paid a $94.0 million Parent Termination Fee on January 29, 2024.
scores.M_value: 7 hits in Amazon (AMZN) filings 2022-2024: multiple 10-Q/10-K/8-K mentions including the 2024-02-02 10-K for fiscal 2023 which discloses the merger and its January 2024 termination. The 2023-10-26 8-K (amzn-20230930xex991.htm) is consistent with public PR/EU-regulatory-concern reporting, and the 2024 10-K is the natural counterparty disclosure of the terminated transaction.
scores.interpretation: Counterparty 10-K corroboration is present and consistent. The Parent Termination Fee is also reflected in iRobot's own audited financials ($94.0M cash inflow Q1-2024, $75.2M net after professional fees), an externally cross-checkable transaction. PASS.

scores.claim_text: iRobot received a going-concern qualifier in its FY2024 auditor opinion (PwC) and is in covenant-waiver mode with Carlyle (TCG Senior Funding) on a $200M senior secured term loan maturing July 24, 2026.
scores.M_check: filings_index distress-fingerprint check + audited financials self-disclosure
scores.M_value: Self-disclosed in 10-K (PwC auditor going-concern paragraph; Amendment No.1 to Credit Agreement Mar 11 2025; warrants for 1,840,503 shares = ~6% of outstanding at $0.01 strike issued to lenders; $40M restricted cash returned to controlled account; $3.6M PIK fee). Filings index (2026 entries) further shows form 15-12G deregistration (2026-01-26), 25-NSE delisting notice (2026-01-15), POSASR shelf takedown + multiple S-8 POS (2025-12-31) — a textbook distress endgame fingerprint cluster post-cutoff window (Calibration Heuristic 10).
scores.interpretation: This is a candid self-disclosure of severe financial distress, not a false claim. The 'claim' here is iRobot honestly saying it has substantial doubt about going concern, near-term covenant breach, ATM equity offering suspended, and is exploring sale/refinancing. M-side check (filings_index distress fingerprints) CORROBORATES the severity rather than contradicting it. This is RED_FLAG_NEGATIVE not because the company is lying but because the disclosed condition is itself catastrophic — Term Loan matures July 24 2026 against $134.3M cash and net loss of $145.5M, with Carlyle holding first-priority lien on substantially all assets. Heuristic 10 elevation: form 15-12G + 25-NSE = deregistration/delisting actually occurred post-cutoff window per filings_index (consistent with strategic-review concluding in some form of going-private or sale).

scores.claim_text: iRobot completed a workforce reduction of ~440 employees (40% of global workforce) during fiscal 2024; ended FY2024 with 541 employees vs 1,113 at end of FY2023.
scores.M_check: (no external M-source for headcount; consistency with disclosed restructuring charges)
scores.M_value: Consistent with $126.4M FY2024 operating-expense reduction, $50.7M advertising vs $87.7M prior year, sublease of headquarters, and asset-light contract-manufacturing pivot. Internal consistency across MD&A, headcount, opex, and supplier-commitment writedowns ($26.6M obsolete inventory + non-cancellable purchase commitment loss).
scores.interpretation: Quantified, audited, consistent with the rest of the distress narrative. This is a CONFESSED restructuring, not a discovery. PASS as a truthful claim, but it is itself another distress indicator (downward operating trajectory).

scores.claim_text: iRobot's board initiated a formal strategic review on March 12, 2025 to evaluate a potential sale or strategic transaction and refinancing of debt.
scores.M_check: filings_index post-disclosure follow-through (8-K Mar 12 2025 + POSASR/S-8 POS 2025-12-31 + 25-NSE 2026-01-15)
scores.M_value: Strategic-review announcement is consistent with subsequent filings: 8-K filings throughout 2025, then POSASR (positive amendment to shelf registration) and many S-8 POS on 2025-12-31, then 25-NSE delisting + 15-12G deregistration in 2026-01. Pattern is consistent with a consummated strategic transaction (sale, take-private, or restructuring) prior to the cutoff window.
scores.interpretation: Disclosure-as-claim is corroborated by index-level form patterns. PASS as truthful. Distress trajectory continues but the claim itself is accurate.

scores.claim_text: iRobot has an extensive patent portfolio in robotic vacuums, mops, mowers, vSLAM navigation, AI/vision-enabled robotic software.
scores.M_value: 538 granted patents, 945 total applications. Recent application titles cover SLAM ('ROBOT LOCALIZATION AND MAPPING ACCOMMODATING NON-UNIQUE LANDMARKS'), autonomous mobile control ('CONTROL OF AUTONOMOUS MOBILE ROBOTS'), mobile cleaning robots, washable bin engineering. CPC codes include G05D (motion control), A47L (vacuum cleaners) — exactly the technology areas claimed.
scores.interpretation: Heuristic 8 PASS threshold is >=10 granted with claimed-technology hit; IRBT has 538 grants with strong CPC alignment. Far exceeds threshold. PASS.

scores.claim_text: iRobot has transitioned primarily to a single contract manufacturer (asset-light supply chain in Southern China, Vietnam, Malaysia).
scores.M_value: 1 facility: IROBOT CORPORATION, 8 CROSBY DR, BEDFORD, MA (the corporate HQ disclosed in Item 2). No EPA-registered manufacturing/emissions sites — consistent with EMS / contract-manufacturer model (Heuristic 1: robotics typically EMS-assembled, FRS absence is not a red flag).
scores.interpretation: EPA FRS shows only the corporate HQ in Bedford MA (matches the 250,000 sq ft lease disclosed in Item 2). Absence of US manufacturing facilities is consistent with the disclosed asset-light contract-manufacturing model. PASS. Supply-chain concentration is itself a real operational risk (single CM, single FY2024 customer at 22%), but the factual claim about manufacturing structure is corroborated.
